name: Harmonized fire record
what: one daily series per area in VIIRS-equivalent "fire cell-days", 2000 to today. Years from the MODIS era are marked "modelled", years from the VIIRS era "observed".
data: FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS; static-source mask; land cover strata.
scores_on: Validity, Relevance. Award: Best Use of Science.
promote: "Satellites changed in 2012 and Romania's fire count quadrupled overnight. We fixed the record."

name: Area selection four ways
what: draw a polygon or box; type lat/lon plus a radius; pick a Romanian county; pick a protected area such as the Danube Delta.
promote: "Any shape, any place: your county, your forest, your farm."

name: Burning calendar
what: heatmap with years as rows and months as columns, 2000 to now, on an accessible sequential ramp; modelled cells hatched. Click a cell for the daily view.
scores_on: Relevance, Presentation. Award: Best Use of Data.
promote: the hero image of the project page and the first frame of the video. "Twenty-five years of fire on one screen."

name: "Is now normal?" card
what: one sentence plus a gauge, e.g. "October 2026: 3rd most active October since 2001, 2.4x the median."
data: feature 1 plus current-month data from the FIRMS API (needs a MAP_KEY; 2026 is not in the country files).
promote: "The question every fire manager asks, answered in one sentence."

name: Exports
what: CSV of the hotspots in the search (with sensor and harmonized fields); CSV of the monthly harmonized table; PNG of the calendar; shareable link that reopens the exact view.
promote: "Take it with you: data for analysts, pictures for reports, a link for the group chat."

name: Accessibility built in
what: colour-blind-safe ramps (viridis-style) with a high-contrast option; every chart has a data-table fallback for screen readers; keyboard navigation; readable on a phone.
scores_on: Validity (user-friendly). The challenge asks for accessible ramps explicitly.
promote: one slide line: "Readable by everyone, including the 1 in 12 men with colour blindness." Check the statistic before using it.

name: "The 2012 cliff" toggle
what: the same chart with raw stitched counts and with harmonized counts; the jump in 2012 appears and disappears.
scores_on: Validity, Presentation. Award: Best Use of Science.
promote: the strongest 5 seconds of the video. Nobody else will show the problem this clearly.

name: Trust meter and uncertainty band
what: a shaded band showing the cross-validated error on every chart, plus a per-area badge ("high trust: 2,400 overlapping detections" / "low trust: too few fires to calibrate").
scores_on: Validity. Award: Best Use of Science.
promote: "We tell you how sure we are." Rare at hackathons and respected by scientific judges.

name: "Not a fire" filter
what: toggle that shows what we removed: industrial heat sources, flares, offshore. Early MODIS has no such flags, so we built our own mask from VIIRS.
promote: "About 8% of what satellites call fire in Romania is a factory chimney. We take it out, even for 2003." (8% is the VIIRS 2015 share; recompute before quoting.)

name: Independent validation view
what: our harmonized yearly totals next to NASA burned area (MCD64A1 / VNP64A1) and EFFIS statistics, with the correlation.
data: burned area products, EFFIS yearly xls.
promote: methods slide: "Checked against two independent records."

name: Satellite timeline strip
what: a thin bar under the calendar showing which satellites were flying each year: Terra only (2000-2002), Terra+Aqua, plus S-NPP (2012), NOAA-20, NOAA-21, and MODIS ending in 2027.
promote: turns a technical problem into a picture anyone understands. Good for the second slide.

name: Open method and open dataset
what: a methods page, a reproducible notebook, and the harmonized Parquet files published for anyone to download.
scores_on: Validity, Impact. Award: Best Use of Data.
promote: "We didn't just build an app, we released the harmonized record."

name: Fire events, not just dots
what: cluster hotspots into events (start, end, duration, footprint) and answer the challenge's own question: "how does a current fire compare with previous ones?" Example: "This fire is the 4th largest in this county since 2000."
promote: "Not 300 dots: one fire, ranked against every fire before it."

name: Fire season clock
what: radial day-of-year chart; per year, season start, peak and length; shows whether the season is shifting earlier or growing longer.
scores_on: Creativity, Presentation. Awards: Art & Technology, Best Storytelling.
promote: the most beautiful visual in the deck. "Romania's fire year used to peak in August. Now it peaks twice, in March and October." (Only if the harmonized data confirms it.)

name: Trend with significance
what: "Burning in this area fell 41% since 2005 (statistically significant)" using a Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, with a plain-language explanation.
promote: gives the anomaly card a long-term companion.

name: "Weather or us?" quadrant
what: for each month, plot the fire weather anomaly (FWI from ERA5) against the burning anomaly. High burning in normal weather points at human behaviour; high burning in extreme weather points at the climate.
data: ERA5 fire danger indices or CEMS GEFF.
scores_on: Creativity, Validity. Award: Best Use of Science.
promote: "Was it the weather, or was it us?" Most creative single idea in this list, and it uses the team's original prediction research.

name: Human fingerprint
what: weekday and holiday pattern of fires. Natural fires don't know it is Sunday; human burning peaks on weekends and around holidays. Lightning fires are rare in Romania, so this exposes how human the fire regime is.
data: FIRMS dates plus the Romanian holiday calendar.
promote: surprising and cheap. "Fires in Romania take the weekend off... or rather, they start then." (Check the direction in the data first.)

name: Policy impact lens
what: policy milestones on the timeline (EU accession 2007, GAEC stubble-burning rules, 2022 fines ordinance) with before/after statistics per area.
promote: "Did the fines work? Now we can measure it." Speaks to ministries, APIA and the Environmental Guard. Claims must stay correlational.

name: Chronic burn sites
what: map of grid cells that burn nearly every year, ranked. Targets for prevention, patrols and farmer outreach.
promote: "These 50 places burn every single year." Concrete and actionable for responders.

name: Land type split
what: calendar split into cropland, forest, grassland and wetland.
data: ESA WorldCover; Corine for older years.
promote: "Stubble, forest or reeds? Three different problems, three different responses."

name: Climatological outlook
what: "Historically, 62% of this area's yearly burning happens in the next 6 weeks", with median and 90th-percentile expectations, next to EFFIS's 6-day danger forecast.
promote: "Plan staff before the season, not during it."

name: Place memory
what: click any point: "This spot burned in 2007, 2012 and 2019."
promote: an intimate demo moment, for example clicking a village in the Danube Delta.

name: Smoke impact
what: estimated smoke emissions per month (CAMS GFAS) and, for a big event, the CO plume (Sentinel-5P); optionally nearby PM2.5 stations.
scores_on: Impact. Award: Global Connection (smoke crosses borders, e.g. Giurgiu to Ruse).
promote: "Fire doesn't stop at the border, and neither does smoke."

name: Cross-border view
what: same calendar for Moldova, Bulgaria and Ukraine, or for an area spanning a border.
data: FIRMS country files for neighbours (verified available).
effort: S once the pipeline is country-agnostic.
promote: proves the method generalizes. Avoid showing conflict-driven fires in Ukraine.

name: Story mode
what: a guided scroll-through: "Romania's burning year", from stubble fires to Delta reed burning to the policy change, with the calendar animating along.
promote: doubles as the slide deck and the video script.

name: Area briefing
what: one printable page for a selected area: calendar, anomaly, trend, chronic sites, outlook.
promote: "What a county inspector puts on the wall in March."

name: Bilingual interface (English and Romanian)
what: language switch. Submission stays in English; Romanian serves the people who would use it.
promote: "Built in Bucharest, for the people who fight these fires."

name: Sensor-agnostic by design
what: the harmonization is a framework: any new sensor is calibrated against the record during an overlap year. Next candidates: Sentinel-3 SLSTR (ESA), MTG FCI (10-minute geostationary over Europe, 1 km), FireSat (data from Q4 2026).
promote: the video's closing line: "MODIS dies in 2027. Your fire history doesn't have to."

name: Alerts
what: subscribe to an area; get notified when weekly activity passes the 90th percentile of its own history.
promote: early warning that is relative to the place, not a global threshold.

name: Embeddable widget and API
what: an iframe calendar that county websites or newsrooms can embed; a JSON endpoint per area.
promote: reach beyond our own site.

name: Field mode
what: offline-capable, low-bandwidth version for phones in the field.
promote: firefighters, not just analysts.

name: One season or two?
what: classify each area's year as having one or two burning seasons, and show when that changed. Two seasons per year is a known human fingerprint (Benali et al. 2017).
data: feature 1; circular statistics on day of year.
scores_on: Validity, Creativity. Award: Best Use of Science.
promote: "Nature burns once a year. Romania burns twice. Here's why." (Only if the data shows it.)

name: Energy view
what: toggle between counting fires and summing their energy (fire radiative power). Energy agrees better between sensors and separates a big forest fire from many small stubble fires.
promote: "Not just how many fires, but how much fire."

name: Return periods
what: "A month this active happens once every 12 years here."
scores_on: Impact (language that emergency managers already use for floods).
promote: borrows a concept managers trust from flood planning.

name: Analog years
what: the past years whose calendar so far looks most like this year's, and what happened next in them.
scores_on: Creativity, Impact (early warning without a trained model).
promote: "This year looks like 2012. In 2012, October was the worst month."

name: Fire regime context
what: which global fire regime ("pyrome") the area belongs to, and similar places elsewhere.
data: Pais et al. 2023 classification, if downloadable.
promote: "Your county burns like [region]; here is what they learned."

name: Seasonal forecast (vision)
what: forecast the coming season's burning from drought indices (as in Turco et al. 2018), shown on the calendar as next year's expected row.
promote: tier 4 pitch: from history to foresight. sites), 17 (human fingerprint), 33 (energy view), 34 (return periods). partners).
